transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... lately, things have just been a bit much. I'm a middle school teacher, and recently the district put this new bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on my plate, right on top of my regular teaching load. 

I mean, I'm still getting through the day, but I just feel so wound up and... discouraged, I guess. It's really not like me. I've even started putting off my lesson plans and ignoring emails that I used to handle without a second thought. It's just starting to feel like I'm not managing it the way I should be.
When exactly did you start feeling this wound-up and discouraged—was it right around the time the new bilingual program was assigned to you, or had you been feeling this way before that?

It was definitely after the new program was assigned. I'd say I started feeling, you know, unlike myself within the first month or two of them adding that rollout to my plate. Before that, I was managing my usual teaching load and everything else pretty well. It just really shifted once that extra responsibility started.
Of the two feelings you described, would you say the anxious, wound-up feeling or the sad, discouraged feeling is the more prominent one for you right now?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's hard to separate them. I think they kind of go hand in hand. 

I feel wound up because I have all this extra work staring at me, and then... well, I get discouraged because I'm just not getting it done like I normally would. So I wouldn't really say one stands out more than the other right now. They're both just sort of there.

Besides feeling anxious and discouraged, have you noticed changes like trouble sleeping, changes in appetite, difficulty concentrating, or feeling excessively worried most of the day, nearly every day?

No, I haven't really noticed any of that. My sleep is fine, and my appetite hasn't changed at all. 

I wouldn't say I'm worried all day long, either. It's really just when I'm looking at that extra workload or thinking about school. And my concentration is mostly okay once I actually force myself to sit down and do something... I've just been avoiding doing it. So, no, none of those other things have really been an issue.
Have you noticed yourself acting out in ways that are out of character—like snapping at colleagues or students, becoming unusually irritable, or breaking rules/routines you'd normally follow?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I'm not snapping at anyone, and I'm definitely not breaking any rules or anything. I'm just... avoiding the extra work when I can. But I'm still treating my students and colleagues the same as always.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or enjoyment in things you used to like doing, or feelings of hopelessness about things in general, not just about the work situation?

No, not at all. I still enjoy the things I usually do outside of school. I'm still reading, spending time with my family... all of that is perfectly fine. 

And I definitely don't feel hopeless about life in general. It's really just tied to that extra workload at school. Outside of that specific situation, everything else in my life is pretty much normal.
